title: Variance and noisy Fourier energy
statement: Let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ have positive variance under the uniform measure, and let $\rho>0$. If $I(f)$ is the sum of the coordinate influences and $\widehat f(S)$ are the Fourier–Walsh coefficients, then $\operatorname{Var}(f)\,\rho^{I(f)/\operatorname{Var}(f)}\leq\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}|S|\rho^{|S|}\widehat f(S)^2$.
replaced: Let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\bbr$ have positive uniform variance, and let $\rho>0$. Writing $I(f)=\sum_S|S|\widehat f(S)^2$, one has $\operatorname{Var}(f)\rho^{I(f)/\operatorname{Var}(f)}\le\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}|S|\rho^{|S|}\widehat f(S)^2$.
